title: Library Imports
content: Imports complex circle theory, basic complex number operations, exponentials, and Mathlib tactics.
mathContext: Uses only basic Mathlib operations: `map_mul` for |z*w| = |z|*|w|, `Complex.abs_ofReal` for |r| when r is real, and `star_mul`/`map_sub` for conjugation distributing over ring operations.

title: Four-Point Ring Identity
content: The identity (z1-z3)(z2-z4) = (z1-z2)(z3-z4) + (z1-z4)(z2-z3) holds in any commutative ring. The proof is a single call to `ring`.
mathContext: This is the algebraic core of the complex-number proof. The identity is purely algebraic -- it holds in Z, Q, R, C, or any commutative ring. No geometry is needed. Expanding both sides and collecting terms gives the same polynomial. The specialization to C is immediate.

title: Cross-Ratio Complement
content: If (z1-z2)(z3-z4) = r*(z1-z3)(z2-z4), then (z1-z4)(z2-z3) = (1-r)*(z1-z3)(z2-z4). This follows from the ring identity by subtraction.
mathContext: The ring identity decomposes the 'diagonal' product into two 'side' products. If one is r times the diagonal, the other must be (1-r) times. This algebraic fact is the key to the absolute-value argument.

title: Ptolemy from Cross-Ratio
content: The central reduction: if the cross-ratio is a positive real r in (0,1), then |z1-z2|*|z3-z4| + |z1-z4|*|z2-z3| = |z1-z3|*|z2-z4|. Proved by: |term1| = r*D, |term2| = (1-r)*D, sum = D.
mathContext: This is the bridge between algebra and geometry. The cross-ratio being a positive real in (0,1) means both summands are positive-real multiples of the same complex number, so |a+b| = |a|+|b|. Uses `map_mul` (|zw| = |z||w|) and `Complex.abs_ofReal` (|r| = r for r > 0).

title: Conjugation of Unit-Circle Differences
content: For |z| = |w| = 1 (unit norm): star(z-w) * (z*w) = -(z-w). The proof uses star(z)*z = 1 and star(w)*w = 1 to simplify the expansion step by step.
mathContext: Since star(z) = z^(-1) for unit-norm z, we have star(z-w) = z^(-1) - w^(-1). Multiplying by z*w: (z^(-1) - w^(-1)) * z * w = w - z = -(z-w). This is the key unit-circle identity that makes the cross-ratio real.

title: Conjugation Cancellation for Products
content: For unit-norm z1,...,z4: star((z1-z2)(z3-z4)) * z1*z2*z3*z4 = (z1-z2)(z3-z4). The z1*z2*z3*z4 factor 'absorbs' the conjugation.
mathContext: Using star_diff_mul_unit twice: star(z1-z2)*(z1*z2) = -(z1-z2) and star(z3-z4)*(z3*z4) = -(z3-z4). The two minus signs cancel: (-1)*(-1) = 1. This means conjugation of any product (z_a-z_b)(z_c-z_d) is 'undone' by multiplying by the product of all four points.

title: Cross-Ratio Self-Conjugacy
content: star(num)*den = num*star(den) where num = (z1-z2)(z3-z4) and den = (z1-z3)(z2-z4). This means the cross-ratio num/den is real.
mathContext: The proof strategy: since star(num)*P = num and star(den)*P = den (where P = z1*z2*z3*z4), both sides of star(num)*den*P and num*star(den)*P equal num*den. Cancelling P (which is nonzero since each z_k has unit norm) gives the result. This is the geometric content of the proof: concyclicity implies real cross-ratio.

title: Ordering Axiom
content: Axiom: for unit circle points in cyclic order, the cross-ratio is a positive real in (0,1). This is the only unproved assumption.
mathContext: The cross-ratio equals sin((t1-t2)/2)*sin((t3-t4)/2) / (sin((t1-t3)/2)*sin((t2-t4)/2)). For t1 < t2 < t3 < t4 < t1+2pi, all sine arguments are in (-pi,0), making all sines negative. The ratio of products-of-negatives is positive. The identity c + (1-c) = 1 forces 0 < c < 1.

title: Ptolemy on the Unit Circle
content: The main theorem: for exp(i*theta_k) in cyclic order, |z1-z2|*|z3-z4| + |z1-z4|*|z2-z3| = |z1-z3|*|z2-z4|. Combines the ordering axiom with ptolemy_from_cross_ratio.
mathContext: The final assembly: the ordering axiom provides a real r in (0,1), and ptolemy_from_cross_ratio converts this into the distance equality. The entire proof chain: ring identity -> cross-ratio reduction -> conjugation argument -> ordering -> Ptolemy.
